message.content:
Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the federal rule is to observe it on the following Monday, which usually creates a 3‑day weekend.)

| Long‑Weekend Dates | Holiday (Observed) | Notes |
|--------------------|--------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day (observed Jan 2) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Family Day is always on the 3rd Monday of February. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Good Friday is a federal holiday on the Friday before Easter Sunday. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day is the Monday preceding May 25. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (observed Jul 3) | Canada Day fell on Saturday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | Labour Day is the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving is the second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day (observed Nov 13) | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day fell on Monday, creating a 3‑day weekend. |

> **Tip for your app** – If you want to support provincial holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, Family Day in Ontario, etc.), you’ll need to pull province‑specific holiday calendars. The table above covers the federal holidays that create long weekends across Canada in 2023.
